t.6.93.1: But Rāvaṇa, deeply enraged out of delusion and driven on by the power of Kṛtānta, his eyes reddened with fury, spoke to his charioteer.
t.6.93.2: As though I were one whose valor had failed, powerless and devoid of manliness, a timid and worthless creature without courage, as if bereft of all fiery energy,
t.6.93.3: Despising me as though I were bereft of magic powers and stripped of my weapons, O fool, you act according to your own judgment.
t.6.93.4: Why, disregarding me and paying no heed to my wish, have you driven this chariot of mine away in the very sight of the enemy?
t.6.93.5: For today, O ignoble one, you have destroyed my glory, my valor, my splendor and the trust others placed in me, all of which I had earned over a long time.
t.6.93.6: While my enemy, famed for his valor and one to be gratified with deeds of prowess, looked on, you have made me, who was eager for battle, into a coward.
t.6.93.7: Since you, out of folly, do not drive this chariot onward, O fool, this suspicion of mine is true: you have been bought over by the enemy.
t.6.93.8: Indeed, this is not the deed of a friend who desires one's welfare; it befits enemies, and this has not been done well by you.
t.6.93.9: Turn the chariot back quickly, before my enemy gets away, if indeed you have dwelt with me, or if my kindnesses are remembered.
t.6.93.10: Thus harshly addressed by the senseless one, the charioteer, whose mind was set on Rāvaṇa's welfare, spoke to Rāvaṇa words that were beneficial and conciliatory.
t.6.93.11: I am not afraid, I am not bewildered, nor have I been won over by the enemies; I am not negligent, nor devoid of affection, nor have I forgotten the honour shown to me.
t.6.93.12: But it was I, desiring your welfare and guarding your fame, my mind overflowing with affection, who did this unpleasant thing, thinking it would please you.
t.6.93.13: O great king, in this matter you ought not, like some petty and ignoble man, regard me as being at fault, for I am devoted to what is dear and beneficial to you.
t.6.93.14: Listen, I shall tell you the reason for which I turned the chariot back in battle, as a river's rushing current is turned back by the waters.
t.6.93.15: I perceive your weariness from the great labor of battle; for, O hero, I do not observe in you either cheerfulness of countenance or delight.
t.6.93.16: And these chariot-horses, wearied from drawing the chariot, are dejected and exhausted by the heat, like cows beaten down by the rain.
t.6.93.17: And the omens that appear to us in great abundance, in each and every one of them as it occurs, I perceive something inauspicious.
t.6.93.18: Place and time must be understood, as well as omens and gestures, dejection, joy and weariness, the chariot-warriors themselves, and their strength and weakness.
t.6.93.19: The high and low places of the ground, its level and uneven stretches, the proper time for battle, and the detecting of the enemy's weak points must all be known.
t.6.93.20: Advancing and withdrawing, holding one's ground and falling back: all this must be known by the charioteer who stands upon the chariot and has charge of it.
t.6.93.21: It was for the sake of rest for you, and likewise for these chariot horses, that I did this fitting thing, sparing you all a dreadful exhaustion.
t.6.93.22: Not of my own will, O hero, was this chariot driven away; what I have done here, O lord, I did overcome by affection for my master.
t.6.93.23: Command me truly, O destroyer of foes; whatever you will say, O hero, that I shall do, with a mind set on freeing itself from its debt to you.
t.6.93.24: Rāvaṇa, pleased by those words of his charioteer, praised him in many ways and, eager for battle, spoke these words.
t.6.93.25: O charioteer, quickly turn this chariot to face Rāghava! Rāvaṇa will not turn back without slaying his enemies in battle.
t.6.93.26: Having spoken thus, Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, was pleased and gave him a single beautiful and excellent ornament for the hand.
t.6.93.27: Then, urged on by Rāvaṇa's words, the charioteer swiftly drove the horses forward, and in an instant the great chariot of the lord of the Rākṣasas stood before Rāma at the forefront of the battle.
